title: Ops Concierge Execution Hub — runbook-as-task runtime and safe automation SDK
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Build an "ops-concierge" execution hub and SDK that turns existing runbooks into first-class, resumable task graphs with RBAC-safe execution, dry-run simulation, idempotency guarantees, and telemetry hooks. The goal is to let support and SRE teams run verified remediation flows in the Console and via a lightweight CLI while preserving auditability and guardrails.

Motivation: Current runbook workflows are fragmented (ad-hoc scripts, docs, and puppet flows). This causes long mean-time-to-repair for known incidents and operational churn when we attempt to automate. The Concierge Execution Hub provides a unified runtime for runbooks-as-tasks that can be embedded in support UIs and gated by role/approval policies.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement policy authoring UI or enterprise RBAC integration (those are separate epics). We will focus on runtime, SDK, and safe-mode integrations.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Runtime model: represent runbooks as directed acyclic task graphs where each node is an idempotent step (shelllet, API-call, or internal helper). Advantages: deterministic replay, partial retries. Trade-off: DAG compilation takes extra validation time; we add a validation pass offline.
- Safety model: three execution modes: "simulate" (dry-run with mocks), "staged" (restricted live with approvals), and "live" (full execution). We will implement a conservative default of staged for all newly onboarded runbooks.
- Idempotency: every step must accept an idempotency token. For legacy scripts we add a wrapper layer that enforces checkpoints and safe-replay semantics.
- Observability: emit structured events (task.started, task.completed, step.error) to the admin-telemetry stream and a short-lived trace in Console. This should allow correlation with incidents and per-step latency breakdowns.
- Telemetry cost trade-off: we will sample verbose step logs for 5% by default and keep aggregated counters for all runs to limit storage. Sampling rate configurable per-project.
- Security: all live-mode executions require a scoped execution role; secrets access must go through KMS-approved wrappers.

Acceptance criteria:
- SDK can compile a simple runbook DSL into a task graph and return a validated execution plan.
- Runtime can run a plan in "simulate" and "staged" modes with correct audit logs.
- Console surface shows run progress (per-step status) with links to logs and trace ID.
- Unit/integration test coverage for step checkpointing and idempotency wrapper.
- Security review completed and sign-off attached.

Testing plan: unit tests for SDK and compiler, integration tests using the synthetic incident harness (see links). Conduct a closed beta with SRE on three curated runbooks (database failover, autoscaler stuck, token-rotation). Follow up with chaos injection (network partitions) to validate safe-replay behavior.
